clue.text: Prepare to fire on a second monster

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise its hammer ready for firing
a trice is an instant, a second

explanation.surface: A gunner readies a shot at some fearsome beast for the second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' reads as an ordinal in the surface but is the noun meaning a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabulous serpent hatched from a cock's egg, whose glance was said to kill: a legendary monster.

clue.text: U.s. showman gives fish to youth leader

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of youth

explanation.surface: An American entertainer hands a fish to the head of a boys' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'youth leader' looks like a scout master; it only asks for the first letter of 'youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cody, 'Buffalo Bill', ran the famous Wild West touring show in America.

explanation.surface: Is a top racing motorist being described?
explanation.walkthrough: The ace in a pack may be of the suit of clubs; a driver is the golf club used off the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: One suit of playing cards is clubs, of which the ace may be one; and a golfer's driver is a type of stick for hitting the ball.

clue.text: Dickensian cricketers made everyone face leg-breaks and not give up

parts.note: all means every person
mug is slang for a face

indicators.note: breaks tells us the word leg is broken up and rearranged
in a down clue, give up means the word not is written upwards, back to front

explanation.surface: A cricket team in a novel faces spin bowling and refuses to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg-breaks' is a spin delivery in cricket, but here 'breaks' scrambles LEG into GLE; 'give up' turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: In Pickwick Papers the Dingley Dell side plays a cricket match against the team from this town.

clue.text: Army is to counter rising in Morocco

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the whole run is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
a bar is a counter in a pub

explanation.surface: Soldiers are ordered to put down an uprising in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like a rebellion; it turns TA + BAR upwards, giving the letters from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Morocco lies on its Atlantic coast, so it is a place found in that country.

parts.note: the Trojan prophetess cursed always to foretell truly but never to be believed

explanation.surface: A woman's predictions proved astonishingly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbelievably' seems to mean astonishingly, but literally nobody believed her.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo's curse on the Trojan princess meant her true prophecies were never credited.

explanation.surface: Someone called Peter is cooking in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Peter's' as 'Pan's', the boy who never grew up; cooking vessels in a kitchen are the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's hero is Peter Pan, so something of his is Pan's; saucepans are cooking utensils.

clue.text: Contracting for a fastener on new net

parts.note: string ties things together, so it is a fastener

indicators.note: new tells us the word net appears in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A clause in a deal about fitting a clip to a fresh net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracting' suggests a business deal, but it means drawing tight; 'new' rearranges NET into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent substance makes body tissue shrink or tighten.

clue.text: Bound, bound to be heard in the main feature

parts.note: to bound is to leap or spring

indicators.note: the second word is spoken, so we take what tied sounds like

parts.note: bound as in tied up

explanation.surface: The headline item in the sea, sure to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea in old poetic English. The two 'bound's differ: a leap, then tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: The very high tides near full and new moon are a feature of the sea, the 'main'.

parts.note: doing something double is doing it twice, repeatedly
the bass is a sea or freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler keeps hooking the same fish, which is toyed with on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' sounds like an angler playing a fish, but it is an instrument being played.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest bowed string instrument of the orchestra, an instrument that musicians perform on.

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the words takes Tarquin's is used

explanation.surface: Someone on stage plays the role of Tarquin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a theatre role, but it signals that the answer is concealed across 'takeS TARquin's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading performer of stage or screen is called a star, and an actor may be one.

clue.text: A song for sixpence ? Try him

definitions.text: A song for sixpence ? Try him

parts.words: A song for sixpence ? Try him
parts.note: the nursery rhyme line sing a song of sixpence, read as asking who sells songs cheaply

explanation.surface: Want a cheap tune? Ask this fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: A sixpence was an old British coin worth half a shilling; street sellers once hawked printed song sheets cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: A monger is a dealer, so this is a seller or hack writer of popular verse songs.

clue.text: What a pity to separate one native from another!

indicators.note: separate shows one piece splitting the other apart from inside

parts.note: a native of Austria
alas is a cry of regret

explanation.surface: A lament at parting two people of different homelands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one native' is an Austrian; 'another' native is the answer, so the definition is just 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Australia and New Zealand region is a native of a second place.

parts.note: Bella is a girl's name

indicators.note: error says the letters of and no have gone astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl is a poisoner, and that is no mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and no error' sounds like an assurance; 'error' scrambles AND NO into DONNA. Bella donna is also Italian for 'beautiful lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade, the toxic plant and its extract atropine.

clue.text: Appointment for Tim and Ian to change in time

indicators.note: in places the rearranged names within the other piece

parts.note: noon is a time of day

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of the two names to be altered in order

explanation.surface: Two men named Tim and Ian get a post that will shift them at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' makes MINATI from TIM and IAN, and 'in' puts it inside NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomination is the act of naming someone for a post.

indicators.note: building means the letters of neat lodge are being constructed anew

explanation.surface: A tidy lodge has a new extension built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the lodge itself, but it signals rebuilding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn out or lengthened has been stretched further.

parts.note: raising a piece of music into a higher key, not a team adding points

explanation.surface: Has a team just increased its tally?
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' reads as a sports tally but is written music, which a musician may shift up a key.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift music into another key, perhaps a higher one, is a musical change of pitch.

explanation.surface: Agree on what an onlooker needs.
explanation.walkthrough: To light on something is to come down and settle on it; anyone looking needs illumination to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird may alight or perch on a branch; eyes need illumination to see anything.

clue.text: Oil spilled about in the river

indicators.note: spilled oil is spread around, so its letters are scattered

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An oil spill pollutes a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' scrambles OIL into LOI.
explanation.definitionFit: France's longest waterway, flowing west to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Left a lot of players a little cash

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
a as in one, a single
d stands for a penny in old British money

explanation.surface: A whole band was left with very little money.
explanation.walkthrough: d was the symbol for the old British penny, the smallest everyday coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserted or forsaken has been left behind.

parts.note: the legendary saint slew a winged beast, whose life fluid he would shed

explanation.surface: Sap shed by England's patron saint.
explanation.walkthrough: St George is the patron saint of England, famed for killing a dragon; the answer is also a red plant resin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark red resin from certain palms and trees, named as if from the beast's veins.

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: a line is a row
the head of red is its first letter

explanation.surface: An argument about a red-haired person aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line; 'over' stacks LINE above R.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger ship sailing a regular route.

clue.text: Pulpit supplied by a Doctor Love

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A preacher's stand provided by a physician called Love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Love' reads as a name, but gives MB and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised reading stand in early churches, like a lectern.

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words house decorating

explanation.surface: No fresh ideas in home decor.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is inside 'hoUSE Decorating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods are not new at all.

indicators.note: back means the word is written in reverse

parts.note: a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: Fleece taken from a beast's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the animal; it reverses LION.
explanation.definitionFit: Noil is the short fibre combed out of wool.

parts.note: pastimes played in a circle of players, but golf too is played as a circuit of holes

explanation.surface: Are links among the pastimes?
explanation.walkthrough: These are party games in which everyone plays for themselves; golf is also played in 'rounds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Party pastimes for any number of players taking part in turn, without teams.

explanation.surface: A monarch related to Queen Charlotte.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Charlotte was George III's wife, but the Charlotte here is the novelist Brontë, whose sister wrote too.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stuart monarch reigned 1702-14; the youngest Brontë sister wrote Agnes Grey.

clue.text: Indian servant accompanies James for security

parts.note: in British India a bearer was a household servant
James Bond, Ian Fleming's spy

explanation.surface: A servant from India travels with someone called James for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'security' looks like a bodyguard, but it is a financial instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond payable to whoever holds it is a financial security.
